scope: Cosmos-Predict2 14B GR00T-Dreams-DROID public baseline on isolated legacy-development episode 60
summary: The SHA-verified 14B task-matched checkpoint completed native 2x2 multiview generation from one real condition frame using pinned precomputed T5 embeddings, but strict continuation quality gates rejected every evaluated view.
evidence: Inference completed 35 sampling steps and produced a 768x432, 16 fps, 93-frame H.264 video with SHA-256 e9969833252717a57234d671b05e5d84bdd30c98caba61be345538999724bd08.
The model received only the real first composite frame, disclosed task text, and precomputed positive/negative T5 embeddings; real future frames were evaluation-only.
Mean first-condition SSIM was 0.9705, confirming correct conditioning, while strict per-view evaluation rejected exterior_1, exterior_2, and wrist continuations.
Aggregate continuation full-frame SSIM was 0.5638, subject edge F1 was 0.6063, motion correlation was 0.2219, and static-anchor SSIM gain was -0.2154.

Contact-sheet inspection found broadly coherent robot appearance and successful block-to-bowl semantics, but texture drift, exterior-view mismatch, and weak wrist-view temporal alignment remain visible.
lessons: Precomputed text conditioning removes redundant per-rank T5 loading and reaches efficient four-GPU context-parallel sampling.
A task-matched public checkpoint is a materially better starting point than the rejected VACE route but is not sufficient for this dataset's exact cameras and identity requirement.
Fine-tuning should emphasize both exterior tiles, keep the inactive tile weight low, and validate motion rather than optimizing only first-frame similarity.
limitations: Only a legacy-development sample was evaluated; no validation or final-holdout sample was used for selection.
This baseline is not accepted for the user-facing demo.
next_actions: Run a two-step four-GPU LoRA smoke test with adapter-only checkpoints, then train and select checkpoints exclusively on the validation split before a single final-holdout evaluation.
